question: Google Timeline history and navigation capabilities that fit a free static Korean event app

sources.observed: Timeline comes directly from devices and is not available in Maps on a computer; use the mobile app.
Android Settings > Location > Location services > Timeline > Export Timeline data. Date-based visits, time editing, individual removal, and opt-in encrypted backups are documented.
Google Maps Settings > Location & Privacy > Export Timeline data > Save to Files; the exported file is named location-history.json.
Timeline is off by default and opt-in. It saves precise locations on devices; particularly personal places have special deletion handling. Other Maps activity is separate.

Maps URLs require api=1 but no API key. origin can be omitted; device location or a start-point form is used. Navigation may be a preview and is not supported for every destination/product. Waypoints are platform-limited and may be ignored.
Published Maps and myactivity.maps scopes do not list Timeline location history. Several Maps activity scopes are restricted; Maps search/activity is not evidence of an actual visit.

Device export differs from old Takeout. Community examples show semanticSegments startTime/endTime and visit.topCandidate.placeLocation.latLng, with rawSignals and activities separately represented. This is not an official stable API schema.
Android device-export parser documents semanticSegments and explicitly distinguishes it from Takeout. No upstream code or personal export was copied.

decisions: Keep Google account access, automatic synchronization, background location tracking, native Navigation SDK, and billed APIs outside this change.
Provide date-based plans and user-confirmed visit history, with repeated visits, per-visit editing and deletion, and browser-only minimal persistence.

Offer optional local JSON import of legacy placeVisit, Android semanticSegments visits, and iPhone visit-array structures. Unsupported variants fail explicitly; no promise of official stable file-schema coverage.
Match only exact venue coordinates within 150 metres and the event period. Reject centroid coordinates. Nearness does not prove attendance: every candidate starts unchecked and must be confirmed.
Never store or send imported raw coordinates, traces, filenames, or unmatched private places. Save only selected catalog event IDs, visit date/time, state, source, and local entry IDs.

Use one Google public-transit URL per itinerary leg, not a multi-waypoint transit request. Keep Naver's optional navigation-app action with a web-search fallback, and coordinate-aware Kakao directions.

live_browser_evidence.source: Local app at http://127.0.0.1:8890, actual published-catalog event detail
live_browser_evidence.observed: Click opened a real Google Maps tab; the loaded destination page displayed transit route choices. No login, purchase, or location permission was submitted. The automatically selected starting point and route text are intentionally not retained.
live_browser_evidence.native_apps: Naver/Kakao native-app launching is not claimed verified on a physical device. Link shape and destination are covered separately by synthetic focused tests.

limits: The app does not calculate a road route, live ETA, turn-by-turn guidance, or historical GPS path.
Real personal exports and Google account data were not used for testing; import compatibility is checked with synthetic files.
Old visits can have no candidate because the current event catalog has a retention window.
Maximum input 20 MiB and 100000 records; preview fails explicitly above 1000 matched candidates.
